transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m just having trouble keeping my mind on one thing. At work, in the warehouse, little things like a beeper or forklift alarm pull me off what I’m counting… and then I’ll realize I put the wrong numbers into inventory.
Did you have this same kind of trouble paying attention when you were a child?
I don’t really remember it being like this as a kid. School was a long time ago… I mean, I got by. Nothing really stands out.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to deal with?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about normal things, but I wouldn’t say it’s a lot when nothing’s going on.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Not really… I mean, I get tired and frustrated, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed.
Did these concentration problems start after something particularly stressful or upsetting happened in your life?
I guess it started maybe about a month ago… around when my husband stopped working outside the home. Our routine changed after that, so… yeah, maybe that had something to do with it.
Since your husband stopped working outside the home, has that change been stressful for you?
A little, I guess. It’s been about a month since he stopped working outside the home, and our usual routine changed. So… yeah, that’s been an adjustment.
Do you find that small noises or activity around you pull your attention away more easily than they used to?
Yeah… more than before, I think. At work, like a beeper or a forklift alarm, even someone moving a pallet, it pulls me off. Then I lose the count and end up putting the wrong numbers in inventory.
Since your routine changed, have you been feeling more on edge?

Yeah… somewhat. Some days I get almost too upbeat, like I’m going to fix everything at home and at work all in one shot. But then if my husband questions it, I can get pretty sharp over something small.
Have you been needing less sleep than usual?
I don’t know… not really that I’ve noticed. My sleep’s a little off sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m needing less, exactly.
Have these concentration problems been causing problems for you at work?

Yeah… a little. I’ve made some inventory mistakes, and I’ve had to go back and double-check with my supervisor, which is embarrassing. It’s not like I’m getting written up or anything, but it’s causing problems.
Before your husband stopped working outside the home, were you having these same concentration problems at work?
Not really, no. It mostly started after he stopped working outside the home… about a month ago, when our routine changed.
Do you find yourself thinking a lot about the change in routine since your husband stopped working outside the home?
I mean… maybe a little, but I don’t sit around thinking about it all day. It’s just different at home now, and I notice it.
Has this change at home been causing you a lot of distress?

Yeah… it’s been stressful. Not, like, constant panic or anything, but my husband and I have been arguing more, and it kind of feels like we’re just trying not to bump into each other at home. And then at work I’m making little inventory mistakes and having to check with my supervisor, so… yeah, it’s been causing some problems.
When you’re away from home, do these concentration problems still feel connected to the change in routine with your husband?

Yeah… even at work it feels tied in, sort of. I’m already off from things being different at home, and then at the warehouse any little thing—like a beeper or forklift alarm, someone moving a pallet—pulls me away from the count. Then I look back and I’ve put the wrong numbers in inventory.
Since this change at home started, have you been feeling anxious?
I don’t know… maybe a little on edge sometimes. I wouldn’t say I’ve been really anxious, exactly. Just… unsettled, I guess.
Does this change at home feel harder for you to cope with than you would expect it should?

I guess… yeah, a little. I mean, I feel like I should be handling it better. But I’m making mistakes at work and having to check with my supervisor, and at home we’re arguing enough that it feels like we’re just walking around each other.
Do you feel your reaction to this change at home has been stronger than you would normally expect for a situation like this?
I’m not really sure. Maybe a little stronger than I’d like, but… I don’t know what’s normal for this, honestly.
Since this change at home started, have you been feeling sad?
Not really sad, no. Maybe just… worn down by it, I guess. But I wouldn’t call it sadness.
Have you been thinking about the change at home a lot?
I don’t know… not a lot, I guess. It comes up, but I try not to sit and think about it too much.
Does your reaction to this change at home feel out of proportion to what happened?
I’m not sure. It feels like… maybe I’m more bothered than I want to be, but I don’t know if I’d call it out of proportion.
